image_prompt.text: A wide main track surface in clean white and silver metallic, sweeping through the multi-section circuit
Glowing blue energy strips running along both edges of the track surface, marking the allowed racing corridor like painted edges on a circuit
The start line drawn across the full width of the main straight, spanned by a futuristic archway gate
The finish gate at the end of the lap — the same sci-fi archway over the start/finish straight, read as the terminal line
A wide starting grid of evenly spaced launch slots marked out across the metallic surface of the start/finish straight
Decorative sci-fi side barriers running the length of the circuit, walls that physically stop a racer leaving the track rather than only indicating the edge
Curved track elements at the circuit's tightest turns, sweeping racers cleanly back around toward the main straight to begin another lap
A tiered grandstand seating area along one side of the circuit, metallic and sci-fi styled, outside the track corridor
Ramps and elevation changes built into the track surface for dynamic racing — climbs and drops along the circuit
A tunnel section the track runs through, lit from within by glowing blue interior lighting
Metallic sci-fi support pillars and structural elements carrying the raised sections of the circuit
Blue energy accents and holographic-style decorations spread throughout the track, barriers and structures

layout_placement.text: The defined position racers begin the lap from, on the grid beneath the start/finish archway
The lap-ending detection zone across the track at the finish archway
Evenly spaced grid slots on the start/finish straight so racers align side by side and launch simultaneously without colliding
Detection regions at the end of each track section and at the main turns, for lap counting, split times, and catching a racer who cut a corner

notes: would have asked: Sounds like a lap-circuit racing layout — a closed loop you run a set number of times, with a starting grid on the main straight, guardrails around the outside, curved turns feeding back into the straight, and lap detection at each section. On top of that I'd build the glowing blue edge strips, the tunnel, the ramps and elevation changes, the tiered grandstand, the support pillars and the start/finish archway you described. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?

would have asked: does the circuit cross over or under itself anywhere? The ramps, tunnel and support pillars hint at it, but the prompt only says elevation changes. If sections do cross, the shape is Multi-Tier Circuit and the route becomes P6 + P2, which is not ready yet — built as a single-layer Lap Circuit for now, and I would note the multi-tier version for when P2 lands.
would have asked: anything else you want in the space?

Shape was a close call between route-circuit and route-multitier; took route-circuit since the prompt states a complete circuit loop with elevation changes but never says the track crosses above or below itself. Kept the Circuit Racing preset shape and all four of its options.

The tunnel is treated as a covered section of the track surface, not an enterable interior, so no P3. Likewise the archway gate and grandstand canopy are dressing over a single-layer route, not overhanging play surfaces, so no P2.
No Universal Option was used. The grandstand is spectator-zone; no crowd or ambient population was requested, so npc-population was not added.

The six requested editable attributes — TrackWidth, TrackLength, NeonColor, SurfaceColor, BarrierHeight, GlowIntensity — are model parameters rather than layout features, and nothing in this handoff can carry them. Passing them on for whoever exposes attributes on the generated model.
No quantities were stated anywhere in the prompt ('multiple curved sections' is not a count), so no pick carries a count.
